title: Ensemble telemetry forecaster for region routing with adaptive fallback policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an ensemble telemetry forecaster that combines short-window p50/p95 estimates, EWMA-based trend smoothing, and a packet-loss/latency link-health score to drive region selection and tiered routing decisions. The forecaster produces a confidence-weighted score per POP and exposes a ranked list of candidate POPs plus recommended fallback model variants and tier (hosted/dedicated) preference. Goal: reduce incorrect cross-region failovers and unnecessary model-variant fallbacks during transient spikes while meeting latency SLOs.
background: Current region selector reacts to raw percentile signals (p50/p95) and an independent network health index. We've observed thrashing during brief congestion (4-10s) and excessive fallbacks to lower-capacity model variants, increasing cost and degrading quality. Proposed solution: fuse signals with a lightweight time-series forecaster and confidence model so routing decisions consider both magnitude and short-term trend/stability.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use a small ensemble: short-window percentile sampler (30s), EWMA trend for p95, and a per-link packet-loss EWMA. This balances responsiveness and noise suppression.
Leverage confidence bands (derived from recent variance) to avoid flip-flopping on low-confidence estimates. If confidence low, prefer local POP or conservative fallback rules.
Compute scores at the POP level with weighted sum: 0.6*forecasted_p95_normalized + 0.3*network_loss_score + 0.1*cost_tier_penalty. Weights tunable via feature flags.
Keep forecasting computation on the aggregator nodes (not per-request) to limit latency overhead; output updated every 5s per POP.
Fallback policy suggests model-variant only when forecasted_p95 exceeds SLO by margin and confidence high for >15s to avoid reaction to spikes.
Tradeoff: longer smoothing reduces thrash but delays detection of persistent degradation. We'll expose hyperparameters and run canaries with different settings.
acceptance_criteria: Forecaster service produces per-POP ranked candidates every 5s and stores last 60s of inputs for auditability.
Region routing uses the forecaster output in a gated rollout for 10% of traffic with canary flags.
Canary shows >=40% reduction in route flips and <=5% increase in 95th percentile latency vs baseline in controlled simulation.
No increase in tail user-facing error rate; DB of recent decisions for debugging available in Console.
Integration tests for signal edge cases (packet-loss burst, p95 spike but p50 stable, cross-POP asymmetric loss) are added to infra-eval.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype forecaster component in Go (30s sampler + EWMA + variance tracker). Add unit tests for stats correctness.
Week 2: Add confidence estimator and weight-based scorer. Instrument aggregator to emit /forecaster/state via internal metrics.
Week 3: Wire forecaster into routing simulation harness. Run synthetic fuzz (network-loss bursts, sustained degradation) and tune weights.
Week 4: Create feature-flagged canary that routes 10% traffic through forecaster decisions; monitor Console dashboards and rollback knob.
Week 5: Post-canary rollout to 50% then global if metrics meet targets. Ship runtime-1.20 with documentation and postmortem playbook.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Forecaster adds CPU/IO to aggregator nodes. Mitigation: efficient streaming aggregator, budget CPU limit, and fallback to legacy selector on overload.
Risk: Overconfident forecasts cause delayed failover. Mitigation: require >=15s sustained high-confidence signal before model-variant fallback.
Risk: Incorrect normalization across POPs with different baseline latencies. Mitigation: normalize p95 by POP baseline median and include regional hysteresis parameter.
testing_plan: Unit tests for percentile sampling, EWMA math, variance/confidence calculation.
Integration tests in routing-sim harness covering 50 scenarios (traffic shifts, loss spikes, asymmetric degradation).
Load test to validate aggregator CPU <10% additional at production traffic levels.
Canary validation dashboards: route flips, p95 delta, fallback count, cost delta, error rate.
monitoring_and_alerting: New Console dashboard: forecaster.p95_forecast, forecaster.confidence, forecaster.score_rank per POP.
Alerts: sustained forecast_confidence_high && forecasted_p95 > SLO_margin for >20s triggers ops notification.
Auto-rollback: if route flips or client error-rate exceed thresholds during canary, toggle feature flag off.
notes: Prototype lives in github.com/redwood-inference/routing/forecaster. Initial branch: feature/ensemble-forecaster-ENG-22001. Confluence spec: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ENG-22001-ensemble-forecaster. Please add performance benchmarks to the PR description.
